summary.text: 妈 means “mother” or “mama.” It is the simplified form of 媽, built from 女 as a female-related meaning component and 馬 as a phonetic component.

formation.text: 媽 combines 女, which contributes a female-related meaning, and 馬, which provides a probable sound cue. In Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese, 媽 *maːʔ and 馬 *mraːʔ share an initial and have broadly similar rhymes, though their vowels differ. 妈 is the standardized simplified form of 媽.

components.text: 女 contributes a female-related meaning in 媽 and 妈.
马 is the standardized simplified form of 馬 within 妈. 馬 is the phonetic component; its older pronunciation resembles 媽 in the cited reconstruction.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese, 馬 *mraːʔ and 媽 *maːʔ share an initial and have broadly similar rhymes, though their vowels differ; this supports a probable phonetic relation.
In modern Standard Mandarin, 馬 mǎ and 媽 mā share an initial but differ in tone. This current resemblance does not establish their historical sound relationship.

history.text: 媽 is constructed from 女 and 馬. The character is not recorded in Shuowen; no earlier paleographic form is established in the cited account.
In the standardized simplified graph 妈, the internal 馬 is written 马.

uncertainties.text: The phonetic analysis has a Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison, but the cited materials do not provide a matched comparison from another reconstruction system. Modern Mandarin readings alone do not establish the historical sound relationship.

senses.text: The character is cited with the meaning “mother” in 龍龕手鑑; the date and exact wording of the cited entry have not been verified from its primary page.

senses.gloss: form of address for female elders, older women, and servants in northern usage
senses.text: Dictionary records include these forms of address, but do not date them or show that they developed from the mother sense.
A dictionary excerpt lists an obsolete “mare” sense as a single-attestation use, without a dated citation linking it to the mother sense.

limitations.text: The recorded senses do not establish a dated path among “mother,” the female-address uses, and “mare,” so no development is inferred.
A secondary account relates 媽 to 母 and proposes an older-language source, but the word history and any semantic path are not established here.
